title: Rav Zevid of Nehardea
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman distinguishes him from Rav Zevid without further designation, as stated explicitly in Kiddushin 72b, where Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: “But in the school of Rav Zevid they do not teach so.” Even so he did not accept it from him, because he had heard it from Rav Zevid of Nehardea; so Rashi explains there. Ameimar received from him, and so we find in Bava Metzia 73b: “Ameimar said: I said the teaching before Rav Zevid of Nehardea.”

Hyman says Rav Kahana (Rav Ashi’s colleague) always told his teaching before him, as in Yevamot 18b and 48b, Ketubot 40a, Bava Kamma 16a and 71b, Bava Metzia 69a, Sanhedrin 69b, Avodah Zarah 63b and Arakhin 6a. Ketubot 63b relates that Rav Zevid’s daughter-in-law rebelled and seized a silk garment … Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi were sitting, and Rav Gamda was sitting with them … he said to them, “Because Rav Zevid is a great man, you flatter him?” According to the author of Dorot HaRishonim, part 3, p. 36a, he is Rav Zevid of Nehardea.

Rav Kahana (Rav Ashi’s teacher) eulogized him in Pum Nahara (not in his presence), as in Moed Katan 27b. Hyman suggests that Nehardea and Pum Nahara were towns near each other, for the author of Erekh Milin states that the town of Drukart was near Nehardea. And we find that the people of Pum Nahara asked Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda, as in Bava Batra 36b, and Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda was in Drukart, as in Taanit 21b.

notes.text: Hyman differentiates Rav Zevid of Nehardea from the unqualified name. The colleague and teacher forms of Rav Kahana remain separately qualified, as in the source. DorotHaRishonim’s daughter-in-law identification and the suggested neighboring towns are attributed; the ErekhMilin reading of the supplied בכל ערוך מלים is disclosed.

Kiddushin 72b directly distinguishes the Rav Zevid school transmission from Ameimar’s Rav Zevid of Nehardea tradition. Ketubot 63b directly names Zevid’s daughter-in-law, Ameimar, Zutra, Ashi and Gamda, but does not itself add Nehardea. The Dorot HaRishonim identification and proposed neighboring towns remain attributed, with Hyman’s two Kahana roles kept distinct.
